Description: Socle technique et applicatif de LEKA : architecture, API, authentification, workspace, multi-tenant, stockage, événements, jobs et services communs.
Interface SaaS globale de LEKA : navigation, sidebar, header, composants UI, états, responsive, accessibilité et langage visuel.
Framework et connecteurs permettant à LEKA d'accéder aux systèmes de l'entreprise : GitHub, Jira, Confluence, cloud, monitoring, bases de données, APIs, etc.
Collecte, extraction, parsing, normalisation, déduplication, validation et préparation des données issues des différentes sources.
Construction du modèle de l'entreprise : applications, services, infrastructure, données, équipes, documentation, processus, incidents, changements, dépendances et relations.
Moteur permettant à LEKA d'identifier, sélectionner et construire le contexte pertinent pour chaque intention, en combinant contexte technique, métier, historique et contraintes.
Maintien et amélioration continue de la connaissance : qualité, fraîcheur, cohérence, enrichissement, détection des changements, nouvelles relations et niveau de confiance.
Expérience centrale LEKA : intention utilisateur → compréhension → analyse → résultat → recommandation → décision → action → vérification → historique.
Couche de capacités permettant à LEKA de mobiliser les bons agents, skills et workflows selon l'intention et le contexte de l'entreprise.
Sécurité et contrôle de la plateforme : permissions, rôles, politiques, validation humaine, secrets, isolation des données, audit, traçabilité, monitoring et observabilité.

h2. Objective

Provide secure user identity and authentication capabilities for LEKA.

h2. User Story

As a user, I want to securely access my LEKA account so that my workspace and data are protected.

h2. Scope

* User registration and login.
* Session management and logout.
* Email verification and password recovery.
* Authentication security controls.
* Authentication-related UI states and errors.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A user can register, verify the account, log in, log out, and recover access.
* Sessions are securely created, maintained, and invalidated.
* Authentication failures return safe, understandable feedback.
* Credentials and session data are protected according to platform security requirements.

h2. Definition of Done

* End-to-end authentication flow implemented and tested.
* Security-sensitive flows covered by automated tests.
* Documentation updated.

h2. Objective

Define the foundational architecture of LEKA so the platform has clear service, module, data-flow, and integration boundaries.

h2. User Story

As a platform engineer, I want a coherent LEKA architecture so that the product can evolve without creating unnecessary coupling.

h2. Scope

* Define core platform components and responsibilities.
* Define service/module boundaries and communication patterns.
* Define synchronous and asynchronous flows.
* Define core architectural principles and technical standards.
* Document key architectural decisions and constraints.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* The main LEKA components and responsibilities are documented.
* Service/module boundaries are explicit.
* Major data and execution flows are documented.
* Architectural dependencies and constraints are identified.
* The architecture is versioned and accessible to the engineering team.

h2. Definition of Done

* Architecture documentation reviewed.
* Key decisions recorded.
* No unresolved critical boundary ambiguity remains.

h2. Objective

Establish workspace and tenant boundaries so each organization can operate securely and independently in LEKA.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want to configure members, roles, and tenant settings so that my organization can use LEKA safely.

h2. Scope

* Workspace creation and configuration.
* Membership and role management.
* Workspace switching.
* Tenant isolation and lifecycle.
* Workspace-level configuration and context.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Workspaces can be created and configured.
* Users can be invited, removed, and assigned roles.
* A user can switch between authorized workspaces.
* Tenant data and permissions are isolated.
* Workspace lifecycle states are handled consistently.

h2. Definition of Done

* Multi-tenant behavior is tested.
* Authorization boundaries are documented.
* Cross-tenant data access is prevented.

h2. Objective

Establish the core data foundation used by LEKA services, knowledge, context, and execution layers.

h2. User Story

As a platform engineer, I want a stable core data model and storage layer so that LEKA can persist and evolve its data safely.

h2. Scope

* Core entities and schemas.
* Database/storage infrastructure.
* Versioning and schema evolution.
* Raw and object storage foundations.
* Data lifecycle and retention hooks.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Core data entities and relationships are defined.
* Persistent storage is available to platform services.
* Schema changes can be versioned and migrated safely.
* Raw/object data can be stored with ownership and lifecycle metadata.
* Retention and deletion rules can be applied.

h2. Definition of Done

* Data foundation is documented and tested.
* Migration strategy is operational.
* Backup/recovery expectations are documented.

h2. Objective

Provide a consistent API foundation for LEKA services and clients.

h2. User Story

As a developer, I want standardized APIs so that LEKA components can communicate predictably and securely.

h2. Scope

* API gateway and routing.
* Authentication and authorization hooks.
* Request validation.
* Response and error standards.
* Versioning, filtering, pagination, and API documentation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* API requests are routed consistently.
* Authentication and authorization are enforced through a common mechanism.
* Invalid requests produce standardized validation errors.
* Responses and errors follow documented conventions.
* APIs support versioning and common query patterns.
* Developer-facing API documentation is available.

h2. Definition of Done

* Core API conventions are documented.
* Representative endpoints are covered by automated tests.
* Security and error-handling behavior is verified.

h2. Objective

Provide reliable asynchronous execution for collection, processing, intelligence, and action workloads.

h2. User Story

As a platform engineer, I want jobs and events to execute reliably in the background so that long-running LEKA processes do not block users.

h2. Scope

* Event model and event bus.
* Queues and background workers.
* Job states and execution history.
* Retry, failure, priority, and scheduling behavior.
* Idempotency and concurrency controls.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Events can be published and consumed reliably.
* Jobs can be queued, executed, monitored, retried, and failed safely.
* Long-running work is decoupled from synchronous requests.
* Duplicate execution is controlled through idempotency/concurrency rules.
* Execution status and history are queryable.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative async workflows tested end to end.
* Failure/retry scenarios tested.
* Operational documentation is available.

h2. Objective

Provide centralized configuration and secure secret management for LEKA environments and services.

h2. User Story

As a platform engineer, I want configuration and credentials managed consistently so that environments remain secure and reproducible.

h2. Scope

* Environment configuration.
* Secure secrets and credentials storage.
* Access control for secrets.
* Rotation and expiration hooks.
* Configuration validation and safe defaults.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Environment configuration is centrally defined and documented.
* Secrets are never stored in application source code.
* Services can access only the credentials they are authorized to use.
* Secret rotation and expiration can be managed.
* Invalid or missing configuration is detected clearly.

h2. Definition of Done

* Configuration and secrets flows are tested.
* Access rules are documented.
* No sensitive values are exposed in logs.

h2. Objective

Establish the operational foundation required to build, deploy, monitor, and maintain LEKA reliably.

h2. User Story

As an engineering team, we want reproducible environments and releases so that LEKA can be delivered and operated safely.

h2. Scope

* Environment management.
* CI/CD pipeline.
* Build, deployment, and rollback processes.
* Platform health checks and monitoring.
* Release and operational management.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Code can move through validated build and deployment pipelines.
* Releases are repeatable and traceable.
* Failed deployments can be rolled back safely.
* Platform health is observable through standard checks and metrics.
* Operational procedures are documented.

h2. Definition of Done

* CI/CD pipeline operational.
* Deployment and rollback tested.
* Basic platform monitoring active.
* Runbook documented.

h2. Objective

Build the shared application shell that provides the consistent frame for all LEKA product experiences.

h2. User Story

As a LEKA user, I want a consistent application shell so that I can navigate and work across the product without relearning the interface.

h2. Scope

* Global header and workspace context.
* Persistent sidebar/navigation frame.
* User/account area.
* Page container and layout rules.
* Shared responsive shell behavior.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* The main LEKA application uses a consistent shell.
* Header and sidebar are available where required by the IA.
* Workspace/user context is visible and accessible.
* Shell adapts to supported desktop/laptop sizes.
* Shell behavior is consistent across major product areas.

h2. Definition of Done

* Shell components are reusable.
* Responsive states are implemented.
* Accessibility basics are covered.
* Visual behavior follows the LEKA design system.

h2. Objective

Define and implement the primary navigation and information architecture of LEKA.

h2. User Story

As a user, I want to understand where I am and where to find each LEKA capability so that I can move through the product efficiently.

h2. Scope

* Primary sidebar structure.
* Section hierarchy and labels.
* Active/inactive navigation states.
* Global search entry in the header.
* Navigation rules for core areas such as Company, Intentions, Activity, and Capabilities.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Navigation reflects the approved LEKA information architecture.
* The primary user entry point for creating an intention is clearly surfaced.
* Current location is always understandable.
* Navigation labels are consistent across the product.
* Search is available globally without competing with the primary intention workflow.

h2. Definition of Done

* Navigation structure is documented.
* All core routes are wired.
* Empty, unavailable, and permission states are defined.

h2. Objective

Create the reusable visual and interaction foundation for the LEKA application.

h2. User Story

As a product team, we want reusable UI components so that all LEKA screens remain consistent, fast to build, and easy to evolve.

h2. Scope

* Typography, spacing, radius, borders, iconography, and visual tokens.
* Buttons, inputs, cards, tables, tabs, menus, badges, tooltips, dialogs, drawers, and pagination.
* Component interaction states and variants.
* Reusable component documentation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Core components exist as reusable building blocks.
* Components expose consistent variants and states.
* Visual tokens are centralized.
* Components support keyboard and focus states where applicable.
* New screens can be composed without creating ad-hoc UI patterns.

h2. Definition of Done

* Component library documented.
* Representative components tested in the application.
* Visual consistency verified across core screens.

h2. Objective

Provide reusable form and interaction patterns for configuring LEKA, entering intentions, selecting context, and confirming actions.

h2. User Story

As a user, I want intuitive inputs and interaction patterns so that I can provide information to LEKA and act on results efficiently.

h2. Scope

* Text inputs, selectors, multi-selects, date/time inputs, and search inputs.
* Intention composer inputs.
* Confirmation, cancellation, and destructive-action patterns.
* Validation and inline feedback.
* Keyboard and focus interactions.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Common input types use standardized components.
* Validation behavior is consistent.
* User actions have clear confirmation or cancellation paths where needed.
* Error and success feedback is understandable.
* Interaction patterns are reusable across product areas.

h2. Definition of Done

* Components are documented and reusable.
* Representative forms and intention flows use them.
* Keyboard accessibility is covered.

h2. Objective

Standardize system states and ensure LEKA remains usable across supported screen sizes and accessibility contexts.

h2. User Story

As a LEKA user, I want clear feedback and a consistent experience across devices so that I can understand system state and continue working without confusion.

h2. Scope

* Loading, empty, error, success, disabled, permission, and offline states.
* Responsive behavior for supported desktop and laptop sizes.
* Keyboard navigation, focus management, semantic structure, and accessible labels.
* Consistent feedback patterns across the application.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Core screens define all relevant system states.
* Responsive layouts remain usable at supported breakpoints.
* Keyboard navigation works for primary interactions.
* Focus states and accessible labels are implemented where required.
* Errors and empty states explain what the user can do next.

h2. Definition of Done

* Core states are covered in the component system.
* Representative screens pass accessibility review.
* Responsive behavior is validated across supported viewport sizes.

h2. Objective

Provide a common connector framework that allows LEKA to securely connect, authenticate, configure, and operate external sources through a consistent model.

h2. User Story

As an administrator, I want connectors to behave consistently so that new enterprise sources can be onboarded without changing the core platform.

h2. Scope

* Common connector lifecycle and configuration.
* Authentication and credential handling.
* Source metadata and capability discovery.
* Connection test and health status.
* Standard connector events and errors.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Connectors follow a common lifecycle and contract.
* Credentials are stored and accessed securely.
* A connection can be tested before activation.
* Connector health and synchronization status are available.
* Failures use standardized diagnostics.

h2. Definition of Done

* Framework documented.
* At least one connector implemented end to end on the framework.
* Connection and failure scenarios are tested.

h2. Objective

Provide reusable UI patterns for representing company data, knowledge entities, relationships, sources, provenance, and quality.

h2. User Story

As a LEKA user, I want complex technical and business information presented consistently so that I can inspect and understand it quickly.

h2. Scope

* Entity cards and detail views.
* Relationship/dependency displays.
* Source and provenance indicators.
* Confidence, quality, freshness, and status indicators.
* Data tables, metadata panels, and knowledge visualizations.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Knowledge entities can be represented consistently across screens.
* Relationships and dependencies have reusable presentation patterns.
* Source/provenance information can be surfaced without ambiguity.
* Quality/confidence/freshness states are represented consistently.
* Components work with empty, partial, and large datasets.

h2. Definition of Done

* Components are reusable and documented.
* Major Knowledge Graph and Company Model views use the shared components.
* Usability and accessibility are verified.

h2. Objective

Connect LEKA to source-code platforms so it can understand repositories, branches, commits, pull requests, issues, and related development metadata.

h2. User Story

As a LEKA workspace administrator, I want to connect our development platforms so that LEKA can build an accurate view of our software estate.

h2. Scope

* GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket support through the connector framework.
* Repository discovery and selection.
* Code/development metadata ingestion.
* Authentication and scope configuration.
* Synchronization status and failure handling.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A supported development platform can be connected securely.
* Repositories can be discovered and scoped for ingestion.
* Relevant metadata is collected according to configured permissions.
* Initial and incremental synchronization are supported.
* Connector status and errors are visible.

h2. Definition of Done

* At least one major code platform works end to end.
* Additional supported platforms use the same framework.
* Permissions and synchronization behavior are documented.

h2. Objective

Connect LEKA to project-management and documentation systems so it can understand work, knowledge, decisions, and operational context.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want to connect our project and documentation tools so that LEKA can correlate technical information with project and business knowledge.

h2. Scope

* Jira, Confluence, Linear, Notion, and equivalent sources through the common connector framework.
* Workspace/project/space discovery.
* Scope and permission configuration.
* Synchronization and status handling.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Supported project/documentation systems can be connected securely.
* Relevant workspaces, projects, spaces, or databases can be selected.
* Documents, issues, metadata, and relationships are ingested according to permissions.
* Initial and incremental synchronization are supported.
* Connection health and ingestion errors are visible.

h2. Definition of Done

* At least one project system and one documentation system work end to end.
* Connector configuration is documented.
* Permission boundaries are tested.

h2. Objective

Connect LEKA to cloud and infrastructure platforms so it can build and maintain an accurate infrastructure view.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want to connect our cloud platforms so that LEKA can understand infrastructure resources, ownership, dependencies, and configuration context.

h2. Scope

* AWS, Azure, and GCP connectivity through the common framework.
* Resource discovery and scope selection.
* Infrastructure metadata ingestion.
* Secure authentication and permissions.
* Synchronization and connection health.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A supported cloud platform can be connected securely.
* Relevant accounts, subscriptions, projects, or resources can be scoped.
* Infrastructure metadata is collected according to granted permissions.
* Initial and incremental synchronization are supported.
* Connection health and permission failures are visible.

h2. Definition of Done

* At least one major cloud provider works end to end.
* Additional providers follow the same connector contract.
* Permissions and scopes are documented.

h2. Objective

Connect LEKA to observability and operations platforms so it can correlate system health, incidents, logs, metrics, and operational changes.

h2. User Story

As an operations user, I want LEKA to access observability data so that analyses can use real operational evidence.

h2. Scope

* Datadog, Grafana, logs, monitoring and incident sources.
* Metrics, events, incidents, alerts, and operational metadata.
* Scope and retention configuration.
* Secure authentication and synchronization.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Supported observability systems can be connected securely.
* Relevant metrics, events, incidents, and alerts can be scoped and ingested.
* Source timestamps and identifiers are preserved.
* Initial and incremental synchronization are supported.
* Connection and ingestion health are visible.

h2. Definition of Done

* At least one observability source works end to end.
* Operational metadata is available to downstream processing.
* Permissions and supported data types are documented.

h2. Objective

Connect LEKA to databases and data platforms so it can understand schemas, data objects, ownership, and technical dependencies.

h2. User Story

As a data or platform administrator, I want LEKA to connect to our data systems so that technical and business context can be correlated.

h2. Scope

* PostgreSQL, MySQL, and compatible database sources.
* Metadata/schema discovery.
* Data object and dependency metadata where permitted.
* Secure credentials and access scopes.
* Synchronization and source health.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Supported database sources can be connected securely.
* Schemas and relevant metadata can be discovered and scoped.
* Access respects configured permissions.
* Initial and incremental metadata synchronization are supported.
* Connection and ingestion status are visible.

h2. Definition of Done

* At least one major relational database is supported end to end.
* Security and permissions are documented.
* Representative schemas are correctly ingested.

h2. Objective

Allow LEKA to integrate systems that are not covered by native connectors through generic APIs and custom integrations.

h2. User Story

As an administrator, I want to connect custom systems so that LEKA can incorporate our proprietary or less common enterprise sources.

h2. Scope

* REST and GraphQL connectors.
* Webhook ingestion.
* Authentication variants supported by the generic framework.
* Field mapping and schema configuration.
* Connection testing and monitoring.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A generic REST or GraphQL source can be configured without code changes to core services.
* Webhook payloads can enter the ingestion pipeline.
* Authentication and secrets use the platform security model.
* Source fields can be mapped to LEKA's normalized structures.
* Generic connector failures are observable.

h2. Definition of Done

* Generic integration path demonstrated with a non-native source.
* Configuration and mapping are documented.
* Security and failure cases are tested.

h2. Objective

Control exactly what each connected source contributes to LEKA and how source data maps into the company model.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want to define source scope and mappings so that LEKA only ingests relevant information and interprets it correctly.

h2. Scope

* Resource/project/repository scope selection.
* Include/exclude rules.
* Source-to-model mapping.
* Field and entity mapping configuration.
* Permission-aware scope validation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Administrators can define source scope before or during activation.
* Include/exclude rules are applied consistently.
* Mapping configuration is persisted and versioned.
* Invalid or conflicting mappings are identified.
* Scope changes affect subsequent synchronization safely.

h2. Definition of Done

* Scope and mapping behavior is tested with representative connectors.
* Configuration changes are auditable.
* Documentation explains supported mappings.

h2. Objective

Provide reliable initial and incremental synchronization plus monitoring for all connected sources.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want LEKA to keep source data current and tell me when synchronization fails so that the company model remains trustworthy.

h2. Scope

* Initial synchronization.
* Incremental synchronization and change detection.
* Scheduling and synchronization status.
* Retry and failure handling.
* Source health and monitoring.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A newly connected source can be synchronized end to end.
* Subsequent changes can be synchronized incrementally where supported.
* Synchronization state and last successful run are visible.
* Recoverable failures can be retried safely.
* Persistent connector problems generate actionable diagnostics.

h2. Definition of Done

* Sync behavior is tested across representative source types.
* Failure and retry behavior is verified.
* Monitoring data is available to operations.

h2. Objective

Build the pipeline that receives data from connected sources and moves it reliably into LEKA processing.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want a reliable collection pipeline so that source data reaches processing without loss or uncontrolled duplication.

h2. Scope

* Intake from connectors.
* Collection jobs and execution status.
* Batching, checkpointing, and backpressure.
* Raw payload persistence and provenance.
* Failure and retry handling.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Connector data can enter a standardized collection pipeline.
* Collection jobs expose status and execution metadata.
* Raw source payloads can be persisted with source and timestamp metadata.
* Failures can be retried without uncontrolled duplication.
* Collection progress is observable.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative connector data flows end to end.
* Failure and retry scenarios are tested.
* Collection contracts are documented.

h2. Objective

Extract useful structured information from raw source payloads so downstream LEKA processing can operate on meaningful content.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want to extract entities, metadata, content, and technical signals from connected sources so that the company model can be built reliably.

h2. Scope

* Extraction from code, documents, APIs, tickets, metrics, and metadata.
* Source-specific extraction strategies.
* Metadata preservation.
* Extraction status, errors, and provenance.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Supported source types produce structured extracted records.
* Source identifiers and provenance are preserved.
* Extraction failures are isolated and observable.
* Extraction results can be passed to parsing and normalization stages.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative source payloads are successfully extracted.
* Error cases are tested.
* Extraction contracts are documented.

h2. Objective

Interpret extracted source content into structures and signals that LEKA can reason over consistently.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want heterogeneous extracted content interpreted into meaningful structures so that downstream models can correlate it.

h2. Scope

* Parsing of structured and semi-structured content.
* Code, document, ticket, configuration, and metadata interpretation.
* Semantic interpretation where required.
* Parsing confidence, errors, and provenance.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Supported extracted content is transformed into structured representations.
* Parsing preserves source identifiers and provenance.
* Unsupported or malformed content is handled without blocking unrelated processing.
* Interpretation results expose confidence or quality information where applicable.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative source types are parsed successfully.
* Failure cases are covered by tests.
* Output contracts are documented.

h2. Objective

Normalize heterogeneous processed data into common LEKA structures so that information from different sources can be correlated consistently.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want data normalized into common structures so that equivalent concepts from different systems can be compared and connected.

h2. Scope

* Common schemas and canonical representations.
* Attribute normalization and type conversion.
* Identifier normalization.
* Timestamp, naming, and format normalization.
* Provenance preservation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Equivalent data from different sources can be represented consistently.
* Canonical identifiers and attributes are applied where defined.
* Source provenance is retained after normalization.
* Invalid or unsupported records are isolated with diagnostics.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative multi-source datasets normalize correctly.
* Mapping rules are documented.
* Automated validation covers key normalization rules.

h2. Objective

Orchestrate the full processing lifecycle from collected data to processed, managed datasets.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want processing stages to execute in the right order with clear state and recovery so that data can move reliably toward knowledge creation.

h2. Scope

* Processing pipeline orchestration.
* Stage dependencies and execution state.
* Parallelism where safe.
* Retry and recovery behavior.
* Processed data storage, versioning, and lifecycle management.
* Execution history and provenance.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Processing stages execute according to defined dependencies.
* Processing state can be inspected and resumed where supported.
* Failures can be retried without corrupting downstream data.
* Processed data is versioned and traceable to source inputs and processing runs.
* Lifecycle policies can govern processed data retention and replacement.

h2. Definition of Done

* End-to-end processing is demonstrated with representative sources.
* Recovery and retry scenarios are tested.
* Processing lifecycle and contracts are documented.

h2. Objective

Identify duplicate records and determine when records from different sources refer to the same real-world entity.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want to resolve duplicate and equivalent entities so that the company model does not contain fragmented or misleading representations.

h2. Scope

* Duplicate detection.
* Cross-source entity matching.
* Identity confidence.
* Merge/link decisions.
* Provenance preservation and conflict handling.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Candidate duplicates can be identified across supported sources.
* Matching uses deterministic and, where appropriate, semantic signals.
* Resolution decisions expose confidence and provenance.
* Conflicts are not silently overwritten.
* Resolved identities are available to downstream modeling.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative cross-source entity cases are resolved correctly.
* False-positive and false-negative scenarios are tested.
* Resolution rules are documented.

h2. Objective

Validate processed data and expose quality signals before it becomes trusted company knowledge.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want data validated for completeness, consistency, freshness, and reliability so that downstream knowledge remains trustworthy.

h2. Scope

* Schema and business-rule validation.
* Completeness and consistency checks.
* Freshness checks.
* Confidence and quality scoring.
* Validation errors, quarantine, and remediation signals.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Processed records are validated against applicable schemas and rules.
* Quality issues are detected and surfaced.
* Invalid records can be isolated without blocking valid data.
* Quality metadata is retained for downstream use.
* Validation results are traceable to the source and processing run.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative datasets pass validation workflows.
* Invalid data scenarios are tested.
* Quality rules and outputs are documented.

h2. Objective

Enrich processed data with additional context, inferred metadata, and relationships before it enters the company knowledge model.

h2. User Story

As the LEKA platform, I want processed records enriched with relevant context so that downstream analysis can operate on richer information.

h2. Scope

* Metadata enrichment.
* Cross-source relationship enrichment.
* Semantic enrichment where useful.
* Ownership and organizational enrichment.
* Enrichment provenance and confidence.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Enrichment can add information without losing source provenance.
* Enriched attributes and relationships expose confidence where applicable.
* Enrichment failures do not corrupt the base record.
* Enrichment outputs can feed Company Model and Knowledge Graph processing.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative datasets are enriched successfully.
* Provenance and confidence are preserved.
* Enrichment behavior is tested and documented.

h2. Objective

Establish the canonical model representing the structure and state of the customer's company inside LEKA.

h2. User Story

As LEKA, I want a coherent company model so that information from different systems can be understood as one enterprise context.

h2. Scope

* Canonical entity model and registry.
* Entity schemas and metadata.
* Entity identity and lifecycle.
* Core company entities and relationships.
* Versioning and provenance.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Core entity types are defined and versioned.
* Entities have stable identities and lifecycle states.
* Source provenance is retained.
* The model can be extended without breaking existing entities.
* Company model entities can be consumed by downstream graph and context services.

h2. Definition of Done

* Canonical model documented.
* Representative entities are created from processed source data.
* Versioning and provenance behavior tested.

h2. Objective

Represent applications, services, environments, ownership, criticality, lifecycle, and technical dependencies in the Company Model.

h2. User Story

As a technology user, I want LEKA to understand our applications and services so that it can reason about their role and dependencies.

h2. Scope

* Application and service entities.
* Environments and lifecycle states.
* Ownership and criticality.
* Application/service dependencies.
* Provenance and source reconciliation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Applications and services can be represented canonically.
* Ownership, criticality, and lifecycle are available where known.
* Environment-specific relationships are preserved.
* Technical dependencies can be represented and queried.
* Source provenance and confidence are retained.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative application landscapes are modeled.
* Cross-source reconciliation is tested.
* Model contracts are documented.

h2. Objective

Represent infrastructure and cloud resources in the Company Model so LEKA can reason about the technical environment and its dependencies.

h2. User Story

As a platform or operations user, I want LEKA to understand infrastructure resources so that analyses can connect applications to the systems that support them.

h2. Scope

* Compute, network, storage, and cloud resources.
* Resource ownership and lifecycle.
* Environment and account/subscription/project context.
* Infrastructure dependencies.
* Provenance and source reconciliation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

As LEKA, I want multiple capabilities orchestrated coherently so that complex intentions can be processed without requiring the user to manage the execution chain.

h2. Scope

* Multi-capability planning.
* Capability dependencies.
* Sequential and parallel execution.
* Shared context and handoffs.
* Failure and fallback coordination.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* A complex intention can invoke multiple eligible capabilities.
* Capability dependencies determine execution order.
* Shared context is passed safely between capabilities.
* Partial failures are represented explicitly.
* Orchestration history is traceable.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative multi-capability scenarios work end to end.
* Dependency and failure cases are tested.
* Orchestration behavior is documented.

h2. Objective

Provide the initial reusable library of enterprise-oriented agents that expose meaningful capabilities through the LEKA runtime.

h2. User Story

As a LEKA user, I want specialized capabilities available behind LEKA so that I can request outcomes without selecting individual agents.

h2. Scope

* Architecture Agent.
* Code Review Agent.
* Security Review Agent.
* Test Agent.
* Debug Agent.
* Documentation Agent.
* Incident Investigation Agent.
* Infrastructure Analysis Agent.
* Data Analysis Agent.
* Release Analysis Agent.
* Build Fixer Agent where applicable.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Each included agent follows the common runtime and capability contracts.
* Agents receive company context through the approved context injection mechanism.
* Tool access is governed by permissions and policies.
* Agent execution, findings, and failures are traceable.
* Agents can be invoked through the Capability Router without exposing implementation details to end users.

h2. Definition of Done

* Initial agent set is registered and executable.
* Representative agents are validated against realistic scenarios.
* Agent contracts and limitations are documented.

h2. Objective

Provide the initial reusable library of enterprise Skills used by agents and workflows.

h2. User Story

As a capability engineer, I want a curated library of reusable skills so that agents can perform specialized operations consistently.

h2. Scope

* Repository analysis skills.
* Code review skills.
* Testing skills.
* Security skills.
* Documentation skills.
* Architecture skills.
* Incident investigation skills.
* Infrastructure skills.
* Data analysis skills.
* Release and deployment skills.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Initial skills are implemented against the common Skill contract.
* Inputs and outputs are explicitly defined.
* Skills can be invoked by agents and workflows through approved interfaces.
* Permissions and execution history are applied consistently.
* Skills expose limitations and required prerequisites where relevant.

h2. Definition of Done

* Initial skill library is registered and executable.
* Representative skills are validated in agent/workflow scenarios.
* Skill catalog and contracts are documented.

h2. Objective

Define the authorization model that controls who can access data, entities, capabilities, and actions in LEKA.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want permissions enforced consistently so that users can only access and perform what they are authorized to do.

h2. Scope

* Authorization architecture.
* Resource and entity permissions.
* Action and capability permissions.
* Permission evaluation.
* Integration with workspace and identity context.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Permissions can be defined for relevant LEKA resources.
* Entity-level access can be enforced where required.
* Action and capability permissions are evaluated before execution.
* Unauthorized access is denied consistently.
* Permission decisions are traceable.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative authorization scenarios are tested.
* Cross-workspace access is prevented.
* Permission rules are documented.

h2. Objective

Provide role and policy management that governs access and behavior across LEKA.

h2. User Story

As an administrator, I want roles and policies applied consistently so that organizational rules are enforced across the product.

h2. Scope

* Role model and management.
* Policy model and policy management.
* Policy evaluation and enforcement.
* Permission inheritance and precedence.
* Policy change history.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Roles can be created and assigned according to workspace rules.
* Policies can be defined, evaluated, and enforced.
* Conflicting policies have deterministic handling.
* Policy changes are traceable.
* Enforcement applies to relevant product and execution paths.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative role/policy scenarios are tested.
* Enforcement is integrated with authorization.
* Policy behavior is documented.

h2. Objective

Define governance controls for consequential LEKA decisions and actions, including risk classification and human approval requirements.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want governance policies to determine when human approval is required so that higher-risk actions remain under explicit human control.

h2. Scope

* Action risk classification.
* Approval requirements and policies.
* Escalation and delegation.
* Governance exceptions.
* Approval policy evaluation.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Actions can be classified according to defined risk levels.
* Approval requirements can be configured by policy.
* Higher-risk actions can require appropriate approval or escalation.
* Delegation and exceptions are controlled and auditable.
* Policy decisions are available to the action execution layer.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative risk and approval scenarios are tested.
* Governance rules are documented.
* Integration with intention/action workflows is verified.

h2. Objective

Protect secrets, credentials, tenant data, and sensitive information throughout LEKA.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want sensitive data and credentials protected consistently so that LEKA can operate securely across enterprise environments.

h2. Scope

* Secret and credential storage/access.
* Encryption in transit and at rest.
* Tenant data isolation.
* Sensitive data detection/classification.
* Access controls and retention enforcement.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Secrets and credentials are stored and accessed through controlled mechanisms.
* Sensitive data is protected in transit and at rest according to platform requirements.
* Tenant isolation is enforced.
* Sensitive data access is permission-controlled and auditable.
* Retention rules can be applied to protected data.

h2. Definition of Done

* Security controls are tested.
* Sensitive data paths are documented.
* No uncontrolled secret or sensitive-data exposure remains in supported flows.

h2. Objective

Govern model access and AI-driven execution so that LEKA uses models and AI capabilities within explicit enterprise controls.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want AI usage and execution constrained by policy so that model outputs and AI actions remain controlled and auditable.

h2. Scope

* Model access policies.
* Usage controls and limits.
* AI output validation.
* AI risk controls.
* Execution policies.
* AI auditability.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Model access can be restricted by workspace, role, capability, or policy.
* Usage controls can limit or govern model execution where required.
* AI outputs can pass through configured validation controls.
* High-risk AI executions can require additional controls or approval.
* AI execution metadata is retained for audit.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative AI governance scenarios are tested.
* Control points are integrated with model and capability runtimes.
* AI governance rules are documented.

h2. Objective

Provide a complete audit trail for important user, data, decision, action, and AI execution events.

h2. User Story

As a workspace administrator, I want LEKA activity to be traceable so that important operations can be investigated and governed.

h2. Scope

* Audit event model and collection.
* User activity audit.
* Data access audit.
* Decision and action audit.
* AI execution audit.
* Search and retention.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Relevant security and product events generate audit records.
* Audit records include actor, timestamp, action, target, outcome, and relevant context.
* Authorized users can search and inspect audit history.
* Audit retention follows configured policies.
* Audit records cannot be modified through normal product flows.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative audit scenarios are verified end to end.
* Audit records are searchable.
* Retention and access rules are documented.

h2. Objective

Provide the operational visibility and resilience needed to run LEKA reliably at enterprise scale.

h2. User Story

As an operator, I want LEKA's infrastructure, connectors, processing, AI executions, and actions to be observable and recoverable so that failures can be detected and handled safely.

h2. Scope

* Application and infrastructure metrics.
* Connector, processing, AI, and action execution metrics.
* Health checks and alerting.
* Failure detection, retry, circuit breakers, and service degradation.
* Backup, restore, and disaster recovery.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

* Core LEKA components expose health and operational metrics.
* Important failure conditions generate actionable alerts.
* Retry and degradation policies are applied consistently where appropriate.
* Backups can be restored through a documented procedure.
* Recovery expectations and critical dependencies are documented.

h2. Definition of Done

* Representative failure scenarios are tested.
* Monitoring and alerting are operational.
* Backup/restore is validated.
* Operational runbooks are documented.
